title: Steady-surge load profile generator & p95 regression watchdog
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a reusable harness that can synthesize long-lived steady-state traffic plus scheduled surge windows to validate Dedicated capacity autoscaling and detect p95 regressions. The harness should model tokens/sec across multiple model families, maintain KV cache priming behavior, support configurable sequence lengths, and produce per-route p50/p95/p99 timelines for regression detection. This ticket covers the harness, a set of canonical scenarios (baseline steady, evening surge, multi-tenant blended), and alerting rules that trigger regression investigations when p95 deviates beyond configurable thresholds. Output artifacts: load trace generator, CI job, Grafana dashboard, and automated nightly regression report.
acceptance_criteria: A harness binary or container image that can replay steady-state load for 8+ hours and inject surge windows with configurable RPS/tokens/sec
Per-route telemetry emitted: tokens/sec, requests/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, backend queue depth, and cache hit ratio
Regression detector task that computes rolling 7-day p95 baseline and raises an alert when current p95 > baseline * 1.2 and absolute increase > 50ms
CI job (perf/steady-surge) that runs nightly and uploads summarized artifacts to S3 with links on the runtime-1.23 release dashboard
Runbook created describing investigation steps and automated data extracts (example query links) for oncall and SRE
End-to-end PR merging harness and dashboard with automated alerting verified on a staging Dedicated cluster
steps_to_execute: Prototype generator: extend perf-trace-sim to add KV cache priming and token-weighted requests (owner: Marco)
Define canonical scenarios: steady-1000tps, steady-2500tps with hourly 30s bursts, evening-peak 3x surge for 10 minutes (owner: Aisha)
Instrument runtime hooks to emit request attributes (model, seq_len, tokens_out) and expose them as Prometheus metrics (owner: infra-team)
Implement p95 baseline computation lambda and a nightly job to persist baselines to S3 (owner: analytics)
Create Grafana dashboard panels and alert rules; wire to Slack #perf-alerts with runbook link (owner: observability)
Add CI pipeline step to run a smoke 1-hour steady-surge in PRs that modify serving runtime or kernel selection (owner: ci)
Run full 8-hour soak on staging Dedicated cluster and validate stability and autoscale events are as expected (owner: Marco)
Postmortem of any regressions and follow-up tickets for root cause fixes (owner: Aisha)
comments: 2025-01-10 | Aisha Patel: Initial write-up and scope. Proposal: keep baseline window at 7 days to reduce noise from infra churn. Suggest we require absolute and relative thresholds to avoid alerts on tiny baselines.

2025-01-12 | Marco Alvarez: Prototype generator added with token-weighted sampling. Found that cold KV cache increases p95 by ~60ms for short sequences; will add optional warmup phase to each scenario.
2025-01-14 | SRE Oncall: Need to ensure harness labels requests so traces map back to tenant IDs. Also request throttling must respect rate limits configured on staging Dedicated clusters.
2025-01-16 | Observability Team: Drafted dashboard panels and alert expressions. Current alert uses increase() on p95 histogram which is noisy; switching to quantile_over_time on aggregated buckets.

2025-01-18 | Marco Alvarez: Ran 4-hour staging soak. Observed autoscaler oscillation when surge windows align across tenants. Added smoothing window to autoscale policy and will re-run full 8-hour test.

2025-01-21 | Aisha Patel: Uploaded summary artifacts from 2025-01-21 run. Baseline computed; two regressions detected (one traced to kernel selection change, one to degraded network perf). Created follow-ups ENG-20510 and ENG-20511.
